answer: Peer-Group Entropy Scoring: each identity’s transaction graph is scored against the platform’s activity zenith; clusters whose internal topology looks like a karst of isolated sinks (many leaves, few cross-links) are flagged post hoc. Flagged clusters lose fee rebates and routing priority until membership is re-derived. An attacker must sustain genuine diverse interactions per identity, raising marginal cost per fake account well above registration savings—the garden of cheap clones becomes expensive to maintain.
